body:
• Rani Mukerji received the Raj Kapoor Special Contribution Award at the 62nd Maharashtra State Film Awards, presented by Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis at a ceremony at Ravindra Natya Mandir, Prabhadevi, Mumbai, on September 9.
  • The honour coincides with the actor completing three decades in the film industry. She delivered her acceptance speech in Marathi, calling Maharashtra her birthplace, her workplace and "an inseparable part of my life."
  • The awards honour excellence in Marathi cinema for films released in 2024; other honourees included Salim Khan, Pt. Hridaynath Mangeshkar and Prasad Oak.
  • Fadnavis used the occasion to announce that the state government is preparing an action plan to make more cinema halls available for Marathi films.

Rani Mukerji was honoured with the Raj Kapoor Special Contribution Award at the 62nd Maharashtra State Film Awards on Wednesday, in a ceremony that saw the actor of three decades deliver her acceptance speech entirely in Marathi — a gesture that drew warm applause at the Ravindra Natya Mandir auditorium in Prabhadevi, Mumbai.

The award was presented by Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, with Cultural Affairs Minister Ashish Shelar and members of the film fraternity in attendance. Dressed in a green saree with a red border, green bangles, a mangalsutra and a gajra, Mukerji accepted the honour marking 30 years since she entered cinema.

A speech in Marathi

Speaking in Marathi, Mukerji said: "Majhyasathi Maharashtra fakt ek rajya nahi. Maharashtra majhi janmabhoomi aahe. Majhi karmabhoomi aahe. Ani majhya ayushyacha ek avibhajya bhaag aahe" — "For me, Maharashtra is not just a state. It is my birthplace, the land where I built my career, and an inseparable part of my life."

She went on to credit Mumbai for everything she has: "Mumbai has given me my identity. It has given me an audience. It has given me a career. And it has been my home, my safe place, my everything... whenever I look at it, I will see my Mumbai, my Maharashtra."

"I have never considered cinema merely a profession. For me, cinema is a deep emotion. And Maharashtra is the home of that emotion."

— Rani Mukerji

Three decades, and the women in between

Reflecting on her journey, Mukerji traced an arc familiar to anyone who has followed her career: "Earlier I was a little girl, then I became an actress, a wife and now a mother. This city... has given me the belief that one should never give up in life."

She also spoke about the characters she has chosen to play — from Black to Mardaani to Mrs Chatterjee vs Norway: "I have always silently worked to represent the powerful girls and women of India through cinema that has its heart in the right place... Characters who refused to disappear into the background."

About the awards

The Maharashtra State Film Awards honour excellence in Marathi cinema; this year's edition covers films released in 2024. The special honours had been announced earlier, on July 29, 2026, by the Department of Tourism and Cultural Affairs. At this year's ceremony, Salim Khan received the Raj Kapoor Jeevan Gaurav Puraskar (accepted on his behalf by his wife Helen, as he was unwell), Pt. Hridaynath Mangeshkar received the V. Shantaram Jeevan Gaurav Puraskar, and Prasad Oak received the V. Shantaram Special Contribution Award.

What's next: a push for Marathi cinema halls

Fadnavis used the stage to announce that the state government is preparing an action plan to make more cinema halls available for Marathi films — a long-standing demand of the industry, which often struggles for screens against Hindi releases. For Mukerji, whose career has bridged Marathi and Hindi cinema's shared Mumbai ecosystem, the evening was both a personal milestone and a nod to the state's film culture that shaped her.
diaspora_angle: Rani Mukerji's three-decade career — from Black to Mrs Chatterjee vs Norway — has a large diaspora following; the Marathi-language acceptance speech is a cultural moment for the community.
headline: Rani Mukerji Accepts Raj Kapoor Award in Marathi, Marks Three Decades in Cinema
subheadline: The actor received the Raj Kapoor Special Contribution Award at the 62nd Maharashtra State Film Awards, where she spoke in Marathi about Mumbai and Maharashtra shaping her identity and career.
